title: Global Economics
completion_message: ¡Formidable! Ahora puedes discutir la economía global como un experto de Davos. Sanctiones, aranceles y monopolios ya no son misterios para ti.

parts.visual:
Los líderes de C2 necesitan entender cómo el mundo afecta sus negocios. 

1. Sanctions (Sanciones): 
- Castigos económicos que un país impone a otro. 
Ej: The UN imposed heavy SANCTIONS on the rogue nation. 

2. Embargo (Embargo): 
- Una prohibición total de comercio con un país. 
Ej: They declared a complete oil EMBARGO. 

3. Tariff (Arancel): 
- Un impuesto sobre bienes importados. 
Ej: The President placed a 25% TARIFF on imported steel.
parts.audio: Welcome to Global Economics and Geopolitics. C2 leaders need to understand how the world affects their business. Number 1: Sanctions. Economic penalties imposed by one country on another to force a change in policy. For example: The UN imposed heavy SANCTIONS on the rogue nation. Number 2: Embargo. An official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country. For example: They declared a complete oil EMBARGO. Number 3: Tariff. A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports. For example: The President placed a 25% TARIFF on imported steel.

parts.visual:
4. Subsidy (Subsidio / Subvención): 
- Dinero que el gobierno da a una industria para mantener los precios bajos o hacerla competitiva. 
Ej: The agricultural industry survives on government SUBSIDIES. 

5. Protectionism (Proteccionismo): 
- Política económica de restringir importaciones para proteger las industrias nacionales. 
Ej: Higher tariffs are a sign of economic PROTECTIONISM. 

6. Trade deficit (Déficit comercial): 
- Cuando un país importa (compra) más de lo que exporta (vende). 
Ej: The USA has a massive TRADE DEFICIT with China. 

7. Monopoly (Monopolio): 
- Cuando una sola empresa controla todo el mercado de un producto. 
Ej: The government sued the tech giant for operating an illegal MONOPOLY.
parts.audio: Number 4: Subsidy. A sum of money granted by the government to assist an industry or business so that the price of a commodity or service may remain low or competitive. For example: The agricultural industry survives on government SUBSIDIES. Number 5: Protectionism. The theory or practice of shielding a country's domestic industries from foreign competition by taxing imports. For example: Higher tariffs are a sign of economic PROTECTIONISM. Number 6: Trade deficit. The amount by which the cost of a country's imports exceeds the value of its exports. For example: The USA has a massive TRADE DEFICIT with China. Finally, Number 7: Monopoly. The exclusive possession or control of the supply of or trade in a commodity or service. For example: The government sued the tech giant for operating an illegal MONOPOLY.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término macroeconómico o geopolítico correcto.

questions.question: To force the dictator to resign, the European Union imposed strict economic ____. (Sanciones).
The US has maintained a trade ____ against Cuba for decades, preventing most commerce. (Embargo).
To protect local car makers, the government put a 30% ____ on all imported vehicles. (Arancel).
Farming is barely profitable, so the government provides a $500 million ____ to farmers every year. (Subsidio).
Raising tariffs to block foreign goods and save local jobs is a policy known as ____. (Proteccionismo).
When a country buys 100 billion in goods from China, but only sells 20 billion to them, it has a massive trade ____. (Déficit comercial).
questions.explanation: Trade deficit = déficit comercial (importas más de lo que exportas).

questions.question: When a single company has absolutely no competition and controls 100% of the market, it is a ____. (Monopolio).
Laws designed to prevent monopolies and promote fair competition are called ____ laws. (Leyes antimonopolio).
The total value of all goods and services produced by a country in one year is its ____ (Gross Domestic Product).
questions.explanation: GDP = Gross Domestic Product (Producto Interno Bruto / PIB).

questions.question: A massive, global corporation that operates in many different countries is an ____ (Multinational Corporation).
When inflation is extremely high and out of control (like 1000% per month), it is called ____. (Hiperinflación).
A country's central bank controls the supply of money and the ____ rates. (Tasas de interés).
The rate at which one currency can be exchanged for another is the ____ rate. (Tipo de cambio).
A situation where a country's exports exceed its imports is a trade ____. (Superávit comercial).
questions.explanation: Trade surplus = superávit comercial (vendes más de lo que compras).

questions.question: An economy where prices and production are controlled by the government (like in the USSR) is a ____ economy. (Economía planificada).
An economy where prices are determined by unrestricted competition between privately owned businesses is a ____ market economy. (Libre mercado).
questions.explanation: Free market economy = economía de libre mercado.

questions.question: The sudden and significant drop in the value of a currency (often done intentionally by the government) is ____. (Devaluación).
The total amount of money that a country's government has borrowed is the national ____. (Deuda nacional).
A prolonged and severe recession (lasting years) is an economic ____. (Depresión).
When a country cannot pay its national debt, it goes into ____. (Incumplimiento de pagos / Default).
questions.explanation: Default = entrar en default, suspensión de pagos.
